<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**A bomb targeting police in [[Dera Ismail Khan]], [[Pakistan]], kills three people and injures five others. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/188771-two-policemen-killed-as-ied-blast-targets-dpos-squad-in-di-khan (Geo News)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**A roadside bomb in [[Syria]] kills one [[United Kingdom|British]] and one [[United States|U.S.]] soldier and injures five more coalition personnel. It is the first death of a British soldier fighting [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/30/british-soldier-killed-ied-syria/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**The government of [[Turkey]] rejects the government of [[France]]'s offer to mediate in the conflict between Turkish armed forces and [[People's Protection Units|Kurdish YPG militia]] in [[Syria]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43595891 (BBC)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**On [[Land Day]], the start of a planned six-week protest at the [[Israel]]i-[[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]n border involving tens of thousands of [[State of Palestine|Palestinians]], Israeli forces kill 16 Palestinians and wound over 1,100 others as tens of thousands of protestors approach the border fence. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/6-gazans-said-wounded-as-thousands-flock-to-border-to-protest/ (''The Times of Israel'')], [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-palestinians-protests/israeli-forces-kill-15-palestinians-in-gaza-border-protests-gaza-medics-idUSKBN1H60AV (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in Italy]]
**In the latest in a series of raids, [[Italy|Italian]] authorities detain 19-year-old Ilyass Hadouz in [[Fossano]] on suspicion of pro-ISIL extremism. [http://www.euronews.com/2018/03/30/moroccan-terror-suspect-detained-in-italy (Euronews)]
**National counter-terror prosecutor Federico Cafiero de Raho states that an estimated 50 people have returned to [[Italy]] after fighting with the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]. [http://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2018/03/30/50-foreign-fighters-in-italy-2_3049e7bd-2499-4142-bbf4-7a43dfc2aded.html (ANSA)]
*Aftermath of the [[Orlando nightclub shooting]]
**A United States court jury in [[Florida]] finds the widow of [[Omar Mateen]] not guilty of assisting her husband in the June 2016 attack that killed 49 people. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/30/us/noor-salman-pulse-trial-verdict/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**Police in [[Germany]] announce that earlier this week they detained four [[Syria]]n nationals on suspicion of arson and attempted murder over a [[Turkish people|Turkish]] [[Muslim]] mosque firebombing in [[Ulm]]. Police say the attack "may have been [[terrorism in Germany|politically motivated]]". [https://www.thelocal.de/20180330/four-syrians-held-for-molotov-mosque-attack (''The Local'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus carrying migrant workers from [[Myanmar]] catches fire near [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], killing twenty people and injuring one other. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/world/thailand-bus-fire-at-least-20-workers-killed-as-doubledecker-bus-goes-up-in-flames-a3802861.html (''Evening Standard'')]
*[[Stansted Airport]] in the [[United Kingdom]] is evacuated after a bus catches fire outside the main terminal. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/30/stansted-airport-evacuated-fire-front-terminal/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*A hot air balloon hits a tree near [[Sydney]], [[Australia]], wounding 16 people. [https://news.sky.com/story/16-hurt-as-hot-air-balloon-crashes-into-tree-in-australia-11309250 (Sky News)]
*An overloaded bus carrying migrants from [[Iran]], [[Pakistan]], and [[Afghanistan]] crashes into a light pole on the Igdir-Kars highway in [[Turkey]] and catches fire. A second bus hits some of the ejected passengers, killing at least 17 people and wounding 36 others. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/bus-crash-in-turkey-kills-17-migrants-from-iran-pakistan-afghanistan/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*An overloaded bus explodes a tyre and crashes near Bhanjyang, [[Nepal]], killing at least two people and wounding dozens of others. A riot follows. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-03-30/nepal-bus-crash-leaves-at-least-two-dead-sparking-riot/9605514 (ABC)]
*The government of [[Russia]] declares a state of emergency in [[Volokolamsk]] over toxic [[hydrogen sulphide]] fumes leaking from a dump at at least ten times permitted concentrations. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43595309 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Russia and weapons of mass destruction]]
**The [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]] announces a second test of its most advanced nuclear [[Intercontinental ballistic missile|ICBM]], the [[RS-28 Sarmat]], from a base in [[Plesetsk]]. President [[Vladimir Putin]] claimed in his March 1 state of the nation speech that the new nuclear arsenal will be impossible for U.S.-engineered technology to intercept. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/russia-tested-nuclear-missile/story?id=54123222 (ABC News)] [https://www.rferl.org/a/putin-set-give-annual-address-amid-presidential-election-campaign/29069948.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Poland|Polish]] [[President of Poland|President]] [[Andrzej Duda]] vetoes a bill that would have demoted all [[communism|communist]]-era military officers who served between 1944 and 1990 to private. [http://www.dw.com/en/poland-president-andrzej-duda-vetoes-bill-demoting-communist-era-officers/a-43200708 (Deutsche Welle)]

;Law and crime
*[[Alcohol licensing laws of Ireland]]
**The government of [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] lifts a 90-year ban on the sale of [[ethanol|alcohol]] on the religious holiday of [[Good Friday]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43592320 (BBC)]
*[[Reactions to the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**The [[Government of Russia|Putin administration]] gives the government of the [[United Kingdom]] one month to reduce its diplomatic missions' sizes to mirror those of the Russian ones in Britain. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/30/russia-summons-british-ambassador-foreign-ministry-give-one/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**The government of [[Russia]] expels 59 diplomats from 23 nations and may also take retaliatory action against four other countries. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/188781-russia-in-spy-rift-riposte-expels-59-diplomats-from-23-countries (Reuters via Geo News)]
**The government of [[Russia]] claims that United Kingdom police searched an [[Aeroflot]] [[Airbus]] jet at [[Heathrow Airport]] arriving from [[Moscow International Airport|Moscow]]. The [[Metropolitan Police]] deny searching the aircraft. [https://news.sky.com/story/russia-say-aeroflot-plane-searched-in-london-by-uk-authorities-11310461 (Sky News)]
*The government of [[Ukraine]] states that it expelled two [[Iran]]ians earlier this year for attempting to buy a [[Kh-31]] missile in [[Kiev]], in violation of [[United Nations]] sanctions. [https://www.thedailybeast.com/ukraine-intel-we-caught-iranians-smuggling-a-ship-killing-missile (''The Daily Beast'')]
*[[Senegal]]ese Judge Malick LaMotte sentences {{ill|Khalifa Sall|fr}}, mayor of [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]], to a five-year term for fraud. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43599055 (BBC)]
*Protestors take to the streets in [[Faisalabad]], [[Pakistan]], following the rape and murder of a local university student. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/188726-protests-mount-over-rape-murder-of-faisalabad-university-student (Geo News)]
*[[Illegal immigration to the United States]]
**[[Mexico|Mexican]] federal police and migration agents find 136 migrants in a locked truck abandoned near a freeway in [[Veracruz]]. Without water or food, the people from the countries of [[Honduras]], [[Guatemala]], [[El Salvador]], and [[Nicaragua]], including dozens of minors, were ''en route'' to the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-immigration/dozens-of-central-american-children-rescued-from-sweltering-truck-in-mexico-idUSKBN1H61M9 (Reuters)]
*[[Immigration to the United States]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] through the [[United States Department of State]] publishes a 60-day notice of request for public comment, proposing to collect [[social media]] [[Online identity|identities]] from nearly everyone who seeks entry into the United States. [http://indianexpress.com/article/world/us-visa-applicants-to-be-asked-for-social-media-history-5117680/ (''The Indian Express'')]
*[[Alexanda Kotey|Alexanda Amon Kotey]] and [[El Shafee Elsheikh]], detained in [[Syria]] on suspicion of beheading hostages for [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]], claim their [[right to a fair trial]] has been breached by the government of the [[United Kingdom]] stripping them of citizenship. [https://news.sky.com/story/is-beatles-pair-hit-out-at-losing-uk-citizenship-11310174 (Sky News)]
*Four suicide bombers attack [[Maiduguri]], [[Nigeria]], killing five people with thirteen others wounded. [http://dailypost.ng/2018/03/31/explosion-rocks-maiduguri/ (Daily Post)]
*[[Terrorism in the United States]]
**Judge [[Ellen Lipton Hollander]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Maryland|U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland]] sentences [[Maryland]] resident Mohamed Elshinawy to a 20-year term for financing [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIS]]. [http://www.foxnews.com/us/2018/03/30/maryland-man-gets-20-years-for-supporting-islamic-state.html (AP via Fox News)]
*U.S. sportswear brand [[Under Armour]] states that the personal details (including user names, email addresses and scrambled passwords) of about 150 million users of the [[MyFitnessPal]] application were compromised in one of the biggest hacks in history. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2018/mar/30/hackers-steal-data-150m-myfitnesspal-app-users-under-armour (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Lansing, Michigan]], [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Lansing|Catholic Diocese's]] insurance company  files a civil suit against Rev. Jonathan Wehrle, former pastor of St. Martha's Catholic Church in [[Okemos, Michigan|Okemos]], a Lansing suburb, for the embezzlement of more than $5 million from his parish. Wehrle already faces six criminal counts for using embezzled funds to pay for home construction (appraised for much more than a $1 million), maintenance, and purchases. [https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/news/local/2018/03/30/insurer-lansing-diocese-files-suit-against-okemos-priest-accused-embezzlement/471649002/ (''Lansing State Journal'')], [http://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/diocese-insurer-sues-michigan-priest-accused-embezzlement-54125005 (AP via ABC News)], [https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/news/local/2017/11/17/okemos-priest-appears-final-day-hearing-embezzlement-charge/871893001/ (''Lansing State Journal''²)]

;Science and technology
*[[Suicide among LGBT youth]]
**''[[Journal of Adolescent Health]]'' publishes research from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] implying that [[transgender]] youths have a much lower risk of [[suicide]] when they are permitted to use their own chosen names. [https://eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2018-03/uota-ucn032818.php (''Eureka Alert!'')], [http://www.jahonline.org/article/S1054-139X(18)30085-5/fulltext (''Journal of Adolescent Health'')]
*[[Chinese space program]]
**Updated predictions suggest that derelict [[China|Chinese]] space station [[Tiangong-1]] will reenter [[Earth]]'s atmosphere over the weekend. [https://www.cnet.com/news/where-chinese-tiangong-1-space-station-could-crash-april-1/ (CNET)]

;Sports
*[[International Olympic Committee]] President [[Thomas Bach]] meets [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]]. [http://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/22967521/ioc-president-thomas-bach-meets-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un (ESPN)]
